RC3 -- the Third Reference Catalogue of Bright Galaxies (de Vaucouleurs et al.
1991) -- via VizieR, catalogue VII/155/rc3, queried 2026-10-11.
The source of every galaxy SIZE in site/src/data/galaxies.js. Positions and
magnitudes still come from SIMBAD (simbad-galaxies.txt); test/galaxies.test.mjs
checks both, field by field.

WHY RC3 AND NOT SIMBAD FOR THE SIZES (#267). SIMBAD's galdim_majaxis is not
one kind of measurement across these fifteen. Against RC3's D25 -- the
diameter at 25 B-mag per square arcsecond, the size NED and most references
quote -- SIMBAD had M 110 at 15% of it, M 32 at 39%, both Magellanic Clouds at
exactly half, M 94 at 62% and M 81 and M 101 near 77%, while Andromeda,
Centaurus A and the Sombrero agreed within a few percent. Drawn at 'true size',
that put M 110 at a sixth of its width. One catalogue, one isophote, for all.

Service: https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/asu-tsv

Query, per galaxy, with that galaxy's SIMBAD position:

  -source=VII/155/rc3  -c=<ra> <dec>  -c.rm=4  -out=_r,name,D25,R25,PA
  -sort=_r  -out.max=1

The nearest RC3 entry within 4' is the galaxy; _r is how far, in arcmin.
D25 is log10 of the major axis in units of 0.1 arcmin, R25 is log10 of
major/minor, PA is the major axis' position angle (degrees east of north,
blank where RC3 has none). maj and min are worked out from them, in arcmin:

  maj = 10^D25 / 10        min = maj / 10^R25
